item.title: Spawn Game Uses Autonomous AI Agents to Ship Code Hourly
item.description:
Spawn Game Uses Autonomous AI Agents to Ship Code Hourly

Spawn, a massively multiplayer gaming environment, is being built and updated by a swarm of AI agents that modify live code and ship changes every hour.

🔍 Overview

  • Players interact with an in‑game agent called Savi by sending prompts that modify the game world.
  • A user report describes creating a castle, summoning a dragon, and riding the dragon around the castle on a phone.

🤖 Autonomous Development

  • Development is driven by a swarm of Fable‑powered agents that cost over $3 million in tokens per month (“we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens”).
  • The agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly.
  • 60 % of work originates from a production error, a Savi bug report, an odd log entry, or a feature request.
  • Savi files bugs herself; when a bug is hit, it is routed to an agent that decides whether it is a real bug, something not to fix, or an intentional design decision.
  • Usually the resulting change is delivered to the user within an hour, accompanied by a message in the same chat.
  • An hour without a ship is treated as a SEV‑0 incident, the most severe kind of incident.
  • Agents can retain only a few hours of work in their “head”; shipping faster helps them stay coherent.
  • A broken change can be rolled back in 30 seconds, exactly where it broke and nowhere else.
  • When a monitor or log alert fires, it starts or wakes an agent that owns the incident, and the team sometimes breaks things on purpose to verify recovery paths.

📊 Model Variants

Model Outcome
Fable 5 / 5.1 Enabled the current level of autonomy (as cited by Jacob).
Opus 5.5 Not sufficient for their needs (“doesn’t quite hack it for them”).
GPT‑6 Astra Applied security fixes by turning off every feature, leaving the product non‑functional.

⚙️ Incident Handling Loop

  • An alert triggers or awakens an agent responsible for the incident.
  • The agent evaluates the bug, classifies it, and either ships a fix or decides on another action.
  • The rapid ship‑and‑rollback capability keeps the production environment tight and responsive.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The system creates a continuous, hour‑long feedback loop that only works because shipping never stops.
  • It demonstrates that a game can serve as a substrate for testing the limits of today’s coding agents.
  • The author notes uncertainty about applying this style to higher‑stakes software, but observes that it is surprisingly effective for a game.
  • Extreme experiments, such as the GPT‑6 Astra security overhaul, highlight both the potential and the risks of autonomous code modification.

#AIAgents #GameDevelopment #AutonomousCoding #SoftwareEngineering

Source: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models

item.title: Reflection AI releases open‑weight model Beam with 5 trillion parameters
item.description:
Reflection AI releases open‑weight model Beam with 5 trillion parameters

Reflection AI announced its first open‑weight base model, Beam, on 5 October 2026 (U.S. time).

🔍 Overview

  • Beam is the inaugural open‑weight model from the NVIDIA‑backed U.S. AI startup Reflection AI.
  • The release came more than six months later than the company’s original target of early 2026.
  • At the time of launch the company’s valuation had risen from $8 billion to $250 billion pre‑money, despite the model not having been released earlier.
  • In the global landscape, Chinese models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, GLM‑5.3 and Qwen 3.8‑Max dominate the open‑weight segment, while U.S. closed‑model leaders remain OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

🧩 How it works

  • Beam uses a Sparse Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) architecture. Although the total parameter count is 5 010 billion, only 230 billion active parameters are used per token.
  • Pre‑training consumed 23.8 trillion tokens.
  • Training relied on NVIDIA GB300 hardware: 6 144 units for pre‑training and 10 500 units for reinforcement learning (RL) over four weeks, generating over 100 million rollouts.
  • Scoring and learning were performed on a sandbox of approximately 1.3 billion entries, with nearly 1 million RL environments prepared.

⚙️ Key details

Attribute Value
Total parameters 5 010 billion
Active parameters per token 230 billion
Pre‑training data 23.8 trillion tokens
Pre‑training compute 6 144 NVIDIA GB300 units
RL compute 10 500 NVIDIA GB300 units (4 weeks)
Rollouts generated >100 million
Sandbox size ~1.3 billion
RL environments prepared ~1 million

💡 Why it matters

  • Beam offers inference quality comparable to GLM‑5.2 while requiring one‑quarter to one‑third of the inference compute thanks to its 23 billion‑active‑parameter design.
  • The model does not claim superiority over current Chinese top models; the company itself notes that models such as Kimi K3 still lead in raw capability.
  • Reflection AI’s broader goal is to provide an “AI Factory” that lets enterprises and governments train proprietary agents using their own data and GPU resources, rather than selling the model itself.
  • The startup was founded in March 2024, is based in Brooklyn, NY, and is expanding hiring across New York, San Francisco, London and Washington DC.
  • Founders Misha Laskin (CEO) and Ioannis Antonoglou (CTO), both former Google DeepMind staff, initially positioned the company around Autonomous Coding – AI that can independently understand, design, modify, test and improve software.
  • In June 2026, during London Tech Week, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced Reflection’s UK expansion plan: over 100 high‑skill hires in the next 12 months and a target of more than 1 000 employees in the UK within three years.

#ReflectionAI #OpenWeight #MoE #AIFactory #AutonomousCoding

Source: NVIDIAが賭ける「米国版DeepSeek」―Reflection AI初の自社オープンウェイト基盤モデル「Beam」の衝撃｜香川友志
